s.g: (vulgar, in the plural) A breast of cup size DD.

dd.f: Abbreviation of day, in two-digit numeric format, as in: dd/mm/yyyy.

dd's.f: Alternative form of DDs; plural of DD

s.g: (sound engineering) A designation on prerecorded compact discs indicating a "full digital recording" (recorded, mixed and mastered in digital).

ddd.f: Initialism of die-deterioration doubling (“a common form of mint-made error on coins that results from degradation of the die used to strike the coin”).

ddj.f: (law, Hong Kong, England, Wales) Abbreviation of deputy district judge.

ddns.f: (Internet) Initialism of dynamic Domain Name System.

ddo.f: (software) Initialism of dynamic drive overlay, a type of computer software; a form of driver.

s.g: (Internet, computer security) A distributed denial-of-service attack, one that originates from many different (geographically and network topographically) sources, on a network of networks such as the Internet.
(Internet, computer security, transitive) To attack by DDoS.

ddosed.f: simple past and past participle of DDoS
simple past and past participle of DDOS

ddosing.f: present participle and gerund of DDoS
present participle and gerund of DDOS

dds.f: (medicine) Initialism of Doctor of Dental Surgery, a terminal higher education degree.

ddt.f: (organic chemistry) Abbreviation of dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, compound originally developed as an insecticide.

s.g: (professional wrestling) a move where a wrestler puts another wrestler into a standing front face lock and then falls backwards, driving the recipient's head into the floor.
